artists.biography: The joining of two of rock's most fearless and experimental musicians seems like a no-brainer -- even more so when considering their pedigrees. In 2015, as his band the Ghost of a Saber Tooth Tiger occupied the opening slot for the Primus tour, Sean Lennon got to play with Primus' virtuoso bassist Les Claypool. An on-stage jam during "Southbound Pachyderm" convinced Claypool that John's son could really play, and the pair decided to collaborate on a new project. The Claypool Lennon Delirium recorded at Claypool's home studio at Rancho Relaxo near Sonoma, California, crafting an unsurprising sound, considering the duo's origins. Their debut single -- the eight-minute mind-bender "Cricket and the Genie" -- shifts and swerves from style to style, exploring the spaces between psych rock, prog, a little acid, a lot of abstract, and even experimental pop. Their debut album, Monolith of Phobos, was released in June 2016. In April of the following year, the band released an exclusive four-song covers EP called Lime and Limpid Green to coincide with Record Store Day.

perplexity.description:
South of Reality is the second studio album by The Claypool Lennon Delirium, a collaborative project between Primus frontman Les Claypool and multi-instrumentalist Sean Lennon. Released on February 22, 2019, the album continues the duo's fusion of psychedelic rock, progressive elements, and experimental pop, building on the foundation laid by their 2016 debut, Monolith of Phobos. Musically, South of Reality is characterized by intricate bass lines, surreal lyrics, and a kaleidoscopic blend of genres, ranging from space rock to art pop. Sean Lennon's drumming, which features prominently on the album, adds a distinctive rhythmic texture, while Claypool's signature bass work and vocal delivery anchor the sound in eccentric, genre-defying territory.

The album stands as a more ambitious and sonically expansive effort compared to its predecessor, with critics noting its maximalist approach and rich production. Uncut praised it as "a meaty maximalist feast, richer and riper than its predecessor," highlighting its layered arrangements and imaginative songwriting. Released on ATO Records, South of Reality further solidified The Claypool Lennon Delirium's reputation for crafting idiosyncratic, genre-blurring rock music. While not a mainstream commercial blockbuster, the album was well-received by fans and critics alike for its creativity and musicianship, marking a significant entry in both artists' discographies.
